newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares down at noon on profit concerns.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares down at noon on profit concerns.

text.p: Shanghai B shares were lower at midday on Monday as institutions sold counters expected to post poor 1997 interim results and took profits on shares which had risen solidly, brokers said.
The B index fell 0.969 point or 1.28 percent to 74.665 on volume of 3.681 million shares worth $1.274 million, compared with $2.334 million on Friday morning.
All listed companies are required to issue interim results by the end of August, but only a handful of them have made the done so.

"Some institutional selling in those stocks that were expected to post poor interim results depressed the market, which made most investors unwilling to make additional purchases despite the recent rebound," said a broker.

"Shares which may have been pushed up in the past few trading days to pave the way for a rights issue also fell today on profit-taking," he said, adding that light selling was able to move prices in a thin market.
"In the interim reporting season, share prices will probably keep the index in a range of 73-78 points," the broker said.
Of 45 B shares, 29 were traded, with 16 down, seven unchanged and six gaining ground.

Shanghai Diesel Engine was the biggest loser, down $0.022 or $0.314 percent to $0.314 on volume of 21,160 shares. Shanghai Jinqiao Export Processing Trade Zone Development followed on concerns over its interim results.
It shed $0.044 or 6.53 percent to $0.630 on volume of 140,747 shares.
Shanghai Erfangji was the most actively traded issue on institutional liquidation, dipping $0.004 or 3.77 percent to $0.102 on volume of 493,000 shares.

Shanghai's A share index fell in sluggish trading, as most investors had little interest in buying at current levels, brokers said. Investors were concerned over possible further measures to dampen sentiment.
The index lost 16.125 points or 1.32 percent to 1,207.915 points on volume of 128.4 million shares worth 1.5 billion yuan.
The SSE30 blue chip index slipped 83.357 points or 2.24 percent to 3,638.342 points.
Shanghai East China Computer Co was the biggest loser on institutional selling, down 0.65 yuan or 5.94 percent to 10.30 yuan on volume of 195,800 shares.
